# @ic-reactor/v4-proto

> Typed, mode-gated handles for Internet Computer canister methods that
> produce TanStack Query options. Each method of a service becomes one handle:
> a read handle gives `queryOptions`, a write handle gives `mutationOptions`,
> and every handle can also be called directly. Built on a module generated
> from the canister's `.did` by `candid-core-cli gen` and on `@icp-sdk/core`'s
> `HttpAgent`. No React dependency: pass the options to `@tanstack/react-query`
> hooks, or to a `QueryClient` anywhere.

This is a prototype. Everything it exports is listed in this file.

## Imports

```ts
import {
  createClient,     // one per app (or per mounted component tree)
  principal,        // checked, branded principal text
  isPrincipalText,  // type guard; never throws
  isReactorError,   // type guard for the one error type handles throw
  type ReactorError,
  type PrincipalText,
} from "@ic-reactor/v4-proto"
import { LedgerService } from "./generated/icrc1.service" // the service descriptor
```

The service descriptor (`LedgerService` here) is generated next to the
candid-core module (`src/generated/icrc1.ts`). It carries every method's
argument types, result types and mode (`query`, `composite_query`, `update`).
Do not edit either file.

## Setup

```ts
const client = createClient({ network, identity })   // a fixed identity
const client = createClient({ network, auth })       // a sign-in source
const ledger = client.canister(LedgerService, { id: "ryjl3-tyaaa-aaaaa-aaaba-cai" })
```

`network` is one of:

- `"ic"` — mainnet (`https://icp-api.io`).
- `"local"` — a replica at `http://127.0.0.1:4943`; its root key is fetched.
- `{ host, rootKey?, name? }` — any replica. A given `rootKey` is used and
  never replaced; without one, the root key is fetched from the replica only
  when the host is local (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`), and never from
  any other host. `name` is the network's name in query keys and defaults to
  `host`.

Give either `identity` or `auth`, not both:

- `identity` — an `@icp-sdk/core` `Identity`, fixed for the client's life
  (scripts, servers, tests). Absent means anonymous.
- `auth` — anything with `getIdentity(): Identity` (the anonymous identity
  while signed out), `isAuthenticated(): boolean` and
  `subscribe(listener): () => void` (called on every sign-in, sign-out and
  principal switch). The client reads it on every call, so it always acts as
  whoever is signed in at that moment.

The client:

| Member                     | What it is                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `client.caller()`          | the current caller's `PrincipalText` (`"2vxsx-fae"`, anonymous, when signed out) |
| `client.isAuthenticated()` | whether a write would be sent now: signed in and not anonymous                |
| `client.subscribe(fn)`     | called when the caller changes; returns an unsubscribe                        |
| `client.network`           | the network's name as it appears in keys                                      |
| `client.canister(svc, { id })` | the handles of one canister                                               |

There is one agent per principal, built on first use and never mutated. A
call made as Alice always goes out through Alice's agent, however the sign-in
state changes while it is in flight.

In React, re-render on caller changes with `useSyncExternalStore`:

```tsx
const caller = useSyncExternalStore(client.subscribe, client.caller)
const signedIn = client.isAuthenticated()
```

Build the client and the handles once (module scope, or `useState` /
`useMemo` in the component that owns them), not on every render.

## Values

Handles take and return the generated module's types with one change:
principals are `PrincipalText` — a `string` brand — in both directions.

| Candid                       | Handle value                                        |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `nat`, `int`, `nat64`, `int64` | `bigint` (never `number`)                         |
| `nat8`..`nat32`, `int8`..`int32`, floats | `number`                                |
| `text`                       | `string`                                            |
| `bool`                       | `boolean`                                           |
| `principal`                  | `PrincipalText`                                     |
| `blob` / `vec nat8`          | `Uint8Array`                                        |
| `opt T`                      | `T \| null` (the property is always present)        |
| `vec T`                      | `T[]`                                               |
| `record { a : T }`           | `{ a: T }` — every field present                    |
| `variant { A : T; B }`       | `{ tag: "A"; value: T } \| { tag: "B" }`            |

Make `PrincipalText` from user input with `principal(text)` (throws a
`TypeError` for invalid text) or narrow with `isPrincipalText(text)`. Values
the library returns — `client.caller()`, principals in replies — already are
`PrincipalText`.

Arguments are always the method's argument tuple, even for one argument:
`handle([arg])`, `handle.queryOptions([arg])`, `mutate([arg])`. A method with
no arguments takes `[]`.

### Results

A method whose single result is a variant with exactly two arms, `Ok`/`Err`
(or `ok`/`err`), is unwrapped: the handle resolves with the `Ok` payload and
throws a `ReactorError` of kind `"canister_err"` whose `.err` is the typed
`Err` payload. Any other result — including a variant with a third arm — is
returned whole.

```ts
// icrc1_transfer : (TransferArg) -> (variant { Ok : nat; Err : TransferError })
const blockIndex: bigint = await ledger.icrc1_transfer([arg])
```

## Reads

Handles of `query` and `composite_query` methods:

```ts
ledger.icrc1_balance_of.queryOptions([account])     // options for useQuery / fetchQuery
ledger.icrc1_balance_of.queryOptions(skipToken)     // no call until you have args
ledger.icrc1_balance_of.queryKey([account])         // the key of those options
ledger.icrc1_balance_of.queryKey()                  // this method's key prefix (current caller)
await ledger.icrc1_balance_of([account])            // call now, no cache
await ledger.icrc1_balance_of.certified([account])  // plain `query` only: as a certified update call
```

```tsx
import { skipToken, useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query"

const profile = useQuery(backend.get_profile.queryOptions(userId ? [userId] : skipToken))
// profile.data: the Ok payload, typed; profile.error: ReactorError<Err> | null
```

`skipToken` is TanStack Query's (`@tanstack/react-query` or
`@tanstack/query-core`); pass it instead of args that do not exist yet.

The key is
`["ic-reactor", network, callerPrincipal, canisterId, method, "query", hex(candid-encoded args)]`.
Because the caller is in the key, one principal's cached answer is never
served to another: after a sign-in, sign-out or switch, the new caller's key
has no data until it loads, and `data` is `undefined` meanwhile. Keep it that
way: options that carry data from one key to the next (`placeholderData:
keepPreviousData`, `initialData` from another key) would show the previous
principal's data.

Reads retry only failures of kind `"not_delivered"`, at most 3 times. You may
add ordinary TanStack options by spreading:
`useQuery({ ...handle.queryOptions(args), staleTime: 30_000, select })`.

`queryOptions` throws `ReactorError` `"invalid_args"` synchronously when the
args cannot be encoded (for example principal text that is not canonical).

## Writes

Handles of `update` methods:

```ts
const transfer = useMutation(
  ledger.icrc1_transfer.mutationOptions({
    invalidates: [ledger.icrc1_balance_of],     // read handles only
    onSuccess: (blockIndex, [arg]) => {},       // optional
    onError: (error, [arg]) => {},              // optional; error: ReactorError<TransferError>
    onSettled: (data, error, [arg]) => {},      // optional
  })
)
transfer.mutate([arg])

await ledger.icrc1_transfer([arg])              // direct call, outside React
```

- `invalidates` lists the reads this write can change. They are invalidated
  (for every caller) after a success, and also after a failure whose
  `mayHaveExecuted` is `true`, because the write may have happened. Nothing
  else is needed to show fresh data after an unknown outcome.
- There is no `retry` option. A write is retried only after a
  `"not_delivered"` failure, which proves the canister never received it; any
  other failure is final. Do not override this: spreading the options and
  adding `retry` re-sends writes that may already have executed.
- A write is sent as whoever is signed in when it runs. If nobody is (or the
  identity is anonymous) it is refused before anything is sent, with kind
  `"unauthenticated"`.
- `mutationOptions()` belongs only to update handles and `queryOptions()` only
  to read handles; the other combination does not type-check.

## Errors

Every failure is one type, `ReactorError<E>`, where `E` is the method's `Err`
payload type (`never` when the result is not an `Ok`/`Err` variant).

| `kind`            | Meaning                                                                    | `mayHaveExecuted` |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `invalid_args`    | the arguments could not be encoded; nothing was sent                       | `false`           |
| `unauthenticated` | a write while not signed in; nothing was sent                              | `false`           |
| `not_delivered`   | the request certainly did not reach the canister (an HTTP 4xx refusal, or reject code 2) | `false` |
| `outcome_unknown` | a write went out and no trustworthy answer came back (network drop, timeout, 5xx) | `true`     |
| `rejected`        | the IC or the canister rejected the call; `.rejectCode` is the IC reject code | `false` for codes 1 and 3 (the IC refused it before any canister code ran); `true` for a write rejected by the canister's own code (4: explicit reject, 5: trap), which may have committed state first |
| `invalid_reply`   | a reply arrived but did not decode as the result type                      | `true` for a write |
| `canister_err`    | the canister returned `Err`; `.err` is typed                               | `false`           |
| `cancelled`       | the caller abandoned the request (an aborted query)                        | `false`           |

Every `ReactorError` also has `message`, `method`, `canisterId` and `cause`
(the underlying agent error, if any).

```ts
try {
  await ledger.icrc1_transfer([arg])
} catch (error) {
  if (!isReactorError(error)) throw error
  if (error.kind === "canister_err") {
    // error.err: TransferError, e.g. { tag: "InsufficientFunds", value: { balance } }
  } else if (error.mayHaveExecuted) {
    // tell the user the outcome is unknown; re-read state before trying again
  }
}
```

In a component, `mutation.error` is `ReactorError<E> | null`; switch on
`error.kind`, and use `error.mayHaveExecuted` to tell "failed" from "unknown".

## Outside React

```ts
import { QueryClient } from "@tanstack/query-core"

const queryClient = new QueryClient()
const balance = await queryClient.fetchQuery(ledger.icrc1_balance_of.queryOptions([account]))
await queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ledger.icrc1_balance_of.queryKey() })
const fresh = await ledger.icrc1_balance_of([account])   // no cache at all
```

Direct calls (`await handle(args)`) never touch a cache; use them in scripts
and services that must always see current state.

## Example

```tsx
import { useMemo, useState, useSyncExternalStore } from "react"
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider, skipToken, useMutation, useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { createClient, isReactorError, type Client } from "@ic-reactor/v4-proto"
import { BackendService } from "./generated/backend.service"

export function App({ auth }: { auth: AuthLike }) {
  const [queryClient] = useState(() => new QueryClient())
  const client = useMemo(() => createClient({ network: "ic", auth }), [auth])
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Profile client={client} />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}

function Profile({ client }: { client: Client }) {
  const backend = useMemo(() => client.canister(BackendService, { id: BACKEND_ID }), [client])
  const me = useSyncExternalStore(client.subscribe, client.caller)
  const signedIn = client.isAuthenticated()
  const profile = useQuery(backend.get_profile.queryOptions(signedIn ? [me] : skipToken))
  const rename = useMutation(backend.set_name.mutationOptions({ invalidates: [backend.get_profile] }))

  if (!signedIn) return <p>Sign in</p>
  if (profile.data === undefined) return <p>Loading…</p>
  return (
    <>
      <p>{profile.data.name}</p>
      <button disabled={rename.isPending} onClick={() => rename.mutate([me, "Ada"])}>Rename</button>
      {rename.error && <p>{rename.error.mayHaveExecuted ? "Unknown outcome" : rename.error.message}</p>}
    </>
  )
}
```

## Do not

- Pass a single argument without its tuple: `handle(arg)` → `handle([arg])`.
- Convert `bigint` values to `number`, or build `PrincipalText` with a cast;
  use `principal()` / `isPrincipalText()`.
- Add `retry` to a write, or call a write from `useQuery`: TanStack Query may
  run a query's function again whenever it refetches, and every run of an
  update executes again.
- Carry data across keys (`keepPreviousData`, cross-key `initialData`).
- Build the client or handles inside render without `useMemo`/`useState`.
- Treat every failed write as "not executed": check `mayHaveExecuted`.
